The @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.522046f606404b2b]{Baali} venerate Ba'al ("Lord") as a being of a thousand faces and a thousand thousand names, and individual @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.522046f606404b2b]{Baali} covens tend to organize around whichever aspect of the Destroyer-god speaks most clearly to them. The best-known orders include:

  • The Destroyer: Militant "Servitors of the Void" who seek an end to all things so their masters might inherit the ashes and begin the cycle anew. Responsible for most of the "bloodthirsty cultist" stereotype attached to the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.522046f606404b2b]{Baali}, and increasingly indistinguishable from mundane Satanic cultism as their zealotry curdles into unreasoning bloodlust.
  • The Celestial: Angelic and demonic scholars who yoke otherworldly beings to their will through millennia of compiled charms and circles, seeking godhead through accumulated knowledge rather than temporal Cainite power struggles. Often found alongside mortal and Cainite occultists, including Cappadocians and @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.jaYCq9rVOh0I9NCN]{Tremere}.
  • The Swarm: The Avatars of the Swarm reject the concept of siring or generation, instead using mortal prisoners as birthing-flesh for insect broods and gathering in subterranean hives. Ironically among the most tolerant of Ba'al's children, since their ideology is one of unifying all oppositions into a single whole.
  • The Mystery: "Children of the Enigma" who turn from society and survival alike to obsess over the ultimate Why of existence, prizing enlightenment above all else; younger Baali sometimes dismiss them as more Cappadocian than Baali.
  • The Multitude: The observation, sometimes advanced by outsiders, that the Baali's internecine ideological squabbles are the sole reason the bloodline has not yet triumphed — the more energy spent on internal strife, the less remains to summon the universal demiurge.

Beneath the orders, lesser servitor-entities such as the plague-lord Decani, unnamed insectile beings, and other embodiments of formless chaos are venerated by individual Baali as intermediaries to the sleeping Ba'al. Those few Cainites granted (and able to endure) direct communion with a slumbering Master are exalted as the shaitan, the highest among the high; lieutenants dispatched on a shaitan's special crusades are known as al'shaitan.

Among the progeny of @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.phgt6OMwTAoAaKfR]{Lasombra}, some whose focus on the darkness within has gradually become an obsession with the darkness without call themselves angellis ater, or "black angels." The particulars of these infernalists' first meeting with the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.522046f606404b2b]{Baali} are unknown, but the unholy alliance has proven strong over recent decades. Azaneal's twelve childer, and their disciples, demonstrate a mastery over darkness thought to be the Magisters' exclusive birthright; at the same time, the courts of Philip of Swabia and Pope Innocent III are known to be rife with @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.phgt6OMwTAoAaKfR]{Lasombra} manipulators, some of whom may be agents of the infernal, and it is whispered that the great Monçada himself consorts with unearthly beings and steely-winged angels behind closed cathedral doors.

Azaneali @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.522046f606404b2b]{Baali} — those infernalists who trade Obtenebration for either Daimoinon or Presence — are more often than not soulless vessels, puppet-husks wandering the world at the whim of their diabolical masters. Some, like Azaneal himself, retain a measure of free will, but their blood is weak: all of Azaneal's childer are sterile and cannot pass on Caine's curse. Azaneal is also a devotee of Via Diabolis (the Road of the Devil) rather than Via Hyron, teaching his followers the precepts of the angellis ater instead — meaning his @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.522046f606404b2b]{Baali} owe no loyalty to the rest of the bloodline, only to themselves and to him. This break from the Road of the Hive's mutual-support ethos is regarded by traditional Baali elders as one of the most damaging developments to strike the bloodline in recent memory.

Nickname: Hyenas. The D'habi are descendants of Nergal's priests. With the supposed death of Nergal (who would later resurface claiming to be Shaitan himself), the other @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.522046f606404b2b]{Baali} orders claimed his priests as a unified ghoul family to serve the entire bloodline, cultivating a separate lineage per order to prevent the ghouls from ever uniting — a precaution that backfired, since every D'habi family was secretly Blood-Oathbound to Nergal all along, making them his spies and assassins within the houses of his rivals. When Nergal reappeared as Shaitan, his hold over the D'habi paralyzed the older orders that suspected the impostor, clearing the way for his crushing (if temporary) rise before his eventual defeat in Crete.

Following that defeat, the surviving younger @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.522046f606404b2b]{Baali} took the D'habi as their own servitors, unaware of the role the family had played in Shaitan's rise. Centuries of harsh servitude and experimentation followed — the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.522046f606404b2b]{Baali} forcing the D'habi to commit acts they could not perform themselves, such as impregnating virgins, devouring sacrificial victims, and serving as vessels for possession — degrading the family to an unimaginable degree. The D'habi now tolerate whatever behavioral aberrations crop up among their own (necrophilia, cannibalism, pederasty, and worse) behind closed doors, since servitude is all they have and anything that threatens it is annihilated.

Appearance: Quiet and reserved in public, most D'habi bear disfiguring marks of harsh upbringing or sexual depravity — torture scars, missing digits, lesions from disease — though the family's diaspora means there is no longer a uniform "type." Their one shared trait is an intense, penetrating gaze.

Family Estates: Once seven estates served the seven Baali orders; only one central estate remains, in Damascus, with dozens of smaller scattered families living in relative squalor.

Disciplines: Dominate, Presence. (Any D'habi found with knowledge of Daimoinon is killed immediately by the Baali.)

Weaknesses: Generations of Dominate and Blood-Oaths at Nergal's hands have left the family weak-willed and highly suggestible; all D'habi suffer a +2 difficulty on all Willpower rolls.

Preferred Roads: Most follow Via Diabolis; Via Hyron is largely forgotten among the younger D'habi.

Family Organization: Strictly age-based, with the eldest surviving D'habi as undisputed head of household.

Baali Duties: The D'habi serve as the Baali's hands in the mortal world — kidnapping victims, digging up graves, robbing churches and temples, assassinating threats, and performing the "mortal touch" portions of Baali rituals (insemination of victims, use of bodily fluids, and the like).

vtmlarp.source: Clanbook: Baali, Chapter Three: Descent into Darkness
